jen_support: FYI customer (ACME) opened a ticket — p95/p99 for text-generation jumped from ~120ms to 1.8s since ~02:12 UTC, multiple 500/503s reported. They say it coincided with an internal deploy. attaching logs soon.
sam_cs: they sent a sample request and a curl: `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` — latencies >3s, occasional 503 body: `{\"error\":\"worker_busy\"}`
oncall-bot: Alert: downstream:inference.queue_length high for tenant acme-prod (alert id: A-9182) at 02:17 UTC
kevin_sre: looking at wavefront panels — admission_queue depth for acme-prod spiked, and worker CPU is fine but many workers show threads blocked waiting on auth-service (calls/sec for /validate-token spiked). suspect auth/identity path is the hotspot.
aziz_runtime: hmm. if auth validation is slow we'll pile requests at the admission queue; that triggers backpressure and then we hit per-worker concurrency limits -> tail latency skyrockets. any recent auth changes in the deploy? liz_eng?
liz_eng: deploy at 02:10 rolled auth-service v2 (opt-in for jwt introspect caching). we gated a cache flag off by default but the rollout unintentionally removed a cache TTL on the introspect path for a subset of requests. logs show DB introspect latency went from 20ms -> 400ms for some tokens.
jen_support: reproduction steps from the customer: repeated requests with same token -> intermittent fast then slow, which matches a cold-cache DB miss.
kevin_sre: quick mitigation options:
- flip rollout (rollback auth-service to previous) OR
- enable local token cache via feature flag for acme-prod tenants (fast)
- temporarily increase inference-worker pod replicas for this tenant routing
- apply tenant-level concurrency cap to spread requests across pools
Which should we do first? :hourglass_flowing_sand:
aziz_runtime: short-term: enable tenant-level fallback pool and increase pool size by +3 to drain queue. also set admission policy to prefer older requests -> drop newest when overloaded? but dropping could be customer-visible.
liz_eng: I can toggle auth cache flag for acme-prod now (scoped flag) — will report after 1 minute.
jen_support: please also add a note to customer that we're investigating and applied a temporary mitigation, ETA 15m.
aziz_runtime: command I'll run for scaling (on-call approved): `kubectl -n prod scale deploy inference-workers-acme --replicas=6` — will also flip routing weight to new pool.
kevin_sre: I'll patch admission controller temporarily to increase per-worker concurrency from 8->12 for acme-prod and extend admission window from 200ms->400ms to allow batching (reduces overhead). Applying now.
oncall-bot: Runbook action logged: scaled inference-workers-acme to 6 (user: aziz_runtime)
liz_eng: toggled auth-introspect-cache=true for tenant acme-prod (feature-flag service), verified cache hits increasing from 12% -> 85% in 30s.
jen_support: customer update sent: "We've enabled a short-term mitigation (token cache + extra worker capacity). We're seeing improved p95; continuing to monitor."
kevin_sre: metrics: p95 fell from ~1.8s -> 260ms after the cache flip + scale. admission queue depth back to normal. leaving extended concurrency for 30m then revert.
aziz_runtime: follow-ups:
- roll a small fix to auth-service to restore proper TTLs (PR#1423)
- add a unit/regression test for introspect cache behavior
- add a tenant-specific fallback pool runbook step in case auth path degrades
- add a metric for token-introspect latency per-tenant to alert earlier
liz_eng: PR opened, will schedule canary deploy to prod-auth tomorrow 02:00 UTC with TTL fix.
jen_support: closing the Slack triage — will reopen if customer sees regressions. thanks! :white_check_mark:
